class.name: TerrainGuide3D
class.brief_description: A hand-drawn guide that [TerrainGenerator3D] reads before erosion: a ridge, a valley or bowl, or a bar of hard rock.
class.description: Place it under a [TerrainGenerator3D] (at any depth) and draw its curve; one curve point is a circle round that point. The generator still makes the relief, so a guided feature drains and looks eroded. Guides are read in tree order, raise guides before lower guides, after the uplift map, [member TerrainGenerator3D.ranges] and basin paths. [b]Raise[/b] lifts the uplift to [member strength] along the line, a raised cosine over [member width]. [b]Lower[/b] scales the uplift down to [member strength] there. [b]Bar[/b] lays rock that rivers and ice wear down only to each curve point's height: the lowest point is the lip where water spills; with [member apron_slope] the right side of the line (looking along it) falls away as a rock slope instead of a sheer wall.

method.name: get_bar_points
method.description: Bar mode: the rock discs the generator holds, as x, level and z, every 32 m along the line (the apron falls away from them on the right).

method.name: get_global_points
method.description: The guide's line in global space (one point: the centre).

members.member: Bar mode: rise over run of the rock slope on the line's right side (1.0 is 45 degrees). 0 leaves a sheer wall wherever the land outside wears down below the bar.
Bar mode: radius of hard rock round each point of the line, in metres.
Whether the generator reads this guide.
Bar mode: distance from the lip, in metres, kept free of the apron so the water falls clear of the face.
What the guide does: raise, lower or bar.
Raise: the uplift along the line (0 to 1, as the uplift map). Lower: the share of the uplift left along the line.
Raise and lower: half width of the band round the line, in metres.

constants.constant: Lifts the uplift along the line: a ridge, range or peak.
Scales the uplift down along the line: a valley, bowl or pass.
Hard rock held at the curve points' heights: a riegel, rock step or lake lip.
